short: The deadliest conflict in human history, fought across six years and every inhabited continent.
full:
The Second World War began on 1 September 1939 with Germany's invasion of Poland, though fighting in China had been under way since 1937. It drew in over a hundred million service personnel and killed an estimated 70 to 85 million people, the majority of them civilians.

It encompassed the Holocaust, the systematic murder of six million Jews and millions of others; the first and only use of nuclear weapons in war; and industrialised destruction on a scale without precedent. It ended with Germany's surrender in May 1945 and Japan's formal surrender aboard USS Missouri on 2 September 1945. The institutions built in its aftermath — the United Nations, the Bretton Woods system, the Genocide Convention — were explicit attempts to make its recurrence impossible.
